alerts.title: EFV CNS toxicity: insomnia and vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines list persistent CNS toxicity including insomnia and abnormal dreams as EFV adverse events requiring management. Patient has been on EFV for ~23 months and reports poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks. EFV is a well-recognized cause of these symptoms. No alternative cause is documented. Guidelines note EFV 400 mg has fewer adverse events than EFV 600 mg, and DTG-based regimens are preferred first-line. The clinician's plan documents the complaint but proposes no management action.

evidence.recommended_action: Consider substituting EFV with DTG, or switching to EFV 400 mg if DTG is contraindicated. Perform viral load test if substituting after six months on ART.

alerts.title: No renal or hepatic monitoring on TDF regimen
alerts.message: Guidelines state that for TDF toxicity, LFTs and RFTs should be done. Patient is on TDF but no renal function tests or liver function tests are recorded. TDF can cause chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, Fanconi syndrome, and hepatotoxicity. Absence of baseline or follow-up renal and hepatic labs represents a monitoring gap that could allow silent toxicity to progress undetected.

evidence.recommended_action: Order renal function tests (creatinine, urinalysis) and liver function tests for patient on TDF-based regimen.

alerts.title: Low-level viremia on current regimen
alerts.message: Guidelines address low-level viremia, noting viral load above suppression thresholds carries risk of subsequent virologic non-suppression and treatment failure. Patient's latest viral load is 60 copies/mL, indicating low-level viremia rather than full suppression. This may signal early adherence issues or emerging resistance, particularly relevant given concurrent EFV CNS toxicity that could impair adherence.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat viral load to confirm trend. Assess adherence and consider regimen review if viremia persists or worsens.
